claim_class: complete projection correspondence in both directions and both modes (4 claims, RPA 7): the same 5,677 retained coordinate pairs observed in every claim with pointwise objective equality; the 4,722 deleted indicators are reconstructed by one simultaneous 18-menu integer lift and, in LP mode, by explicit fractional endpoint masses on three coordinates per block.
claims: 1. Forward integer (reverse=false, input/output_integers=true, objective=Equal, projection=5,677 pairs): every source MI point maps to a target MI point with every retained coordinate and the objective unchanged; only the 36 added rows are new content (37,256 obligations).

2. Reverse integer (reverse=true, integer mode): one simultaneous MenuLift of 18 MenuWitnesses generates 4,722 binary option variables plus 36 rows, reconstructing all 4,722 deleted indicators and re-deriving all 54 deleted source rows (51,440 obligations).
3. Forward continuous (reverse=false, LP mode): the same Lin-only proof as claim 1 with no integrality observations (31,603 obligations).

4. Reverse continuous (reverse=true, LP mode): a 10,399-entry Return map; per block only the two endpoint options get nonzero masses ((U-x-(U-c)g)/(U-L), (x-L-(c-L)g)/(U-L)) and the distinguished option maps to g, the other 4,668 deleted coordinates map to the constant zero (41,065 obligations).
5. All four claims carry the identical 5,677-pair list; request.json is exactly that 4-claim array (264,236 B) while proof.rpa also carries the blocks (4,820,431 B).
proof_encoding: Single RPA 7 certificate with exactly one Block per Claim in claim order: 4,820,431 B text, assembles to 3,109,066 B RPX; verify runs 4 claims, 161,364 obligations, work 2,314,608, 54 branches, peak live facts 72.

Blocks 0 and 2 (forward): 36 Lin steps each (191-382 terms, 9,480 terms total) derive the 36 added rows from the three block rows plus per-indicator VarLower facts, then a Return with a 5,677-entry identity map and 5,678 literal Exact checks.

Block 1 (reverse integer): MenuLift of 18 menus (maximum_index in {189,215,380}, activation constant 1, index = x-L, exactly six premises each) whose body Return map covers all 10,399 source coordinates (5,677 identities plus 4,722 menu variables).

Block 3 (reverse LP): 72 Lin steps (endpoint nonnegativity from the added rows) and a 10,399-entry Return map with three nonzero affine expressions per block; deleted sum and value rows are discharged by the menu sum/moment rows and the 18 link rows by Cases/Absurd/Witness.

Deleted coordinates are never observed in the forward claims (they are not in the projection list); they appear there only as VarLower premises of the added-row derivations (tools/prepare_test13.py:31-32).
reformulation: Delete 18 private one-hot blocks, each (sum_v y_v = 1, x = sum_v v*y_v, g <= y_c) with binary y over a consecutive integer interval [L,U] and L<c<U, and replace each by two inequalities -x+(c-L)g <= -L and x+(U-c)g <= U: 4,722 binaries and 54 rows out, 36 rows in. Variables 10,399 -> 5,677 (nonzeros 44,959 -> 35,545) while rows barely move 14,589 -> 14,571; solver outcome Optimal/125,055 -> Optimal/125,055.
agent_manual_work: Hand-written exact MPS parser (fractions.Fraction) over the 78,046-line file plus a full census: one N row, 14,423 L and 166 E rows, 28 INTORG/INTEND markers, 10,385 UP / 74 LO / 14 FX records, one RHS vector, no RANGES/OBJSENSE, objective coefficient 1 on column obj.

Block discovery by incidence: 18 equalities of 381/190/216 unit coefficients, complete column-incidence privacy checks (each candidate occurs only in its sum row, value row and one link row), exhaustive integer-domain coverage and no objective contribution.

Exhaustive local witness search: 9,444 (x,g) assignments, 4,740 feasible lifts, 4,704 trigger exclusions, forward inequalities re-checked over every represented value; plus 400 box-implied rows and an implication graph of 4,555 arcs / 69 SCCs.

Independent auditor output/verify.py (10,994 B) and output/audit.json (368,671 B): Decimal re-parse, SHA-256 binding, exact retained/deleted column sets, per-row and per-coordinate equality, 18 simultaneous reconstructions, all 5,677 retained bounds and integrality flags.

Structure searches and the SCC step were hand-rolled (import networkx failed), so candidate discovery for the noncommitted redundancy/alias families was done with bespoke code rather than any kernel query.
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test13.py (114 lines): parses both MPS files via prepare_affine.parse_mps, asserts the target diff by name, builds the 36 Lin derivations, the 18-menu extension, the nested link-row Cases proof and the four mutation attacks.

Eight imported sibling modules totalling 1,392 lines: prepare_affine (233), prepare_test40 (207), prepare_test57 (103), prepare_test88 (233), prepare_test19 (155), prepare_test23 (163), prepare_test54 (203), menu_injectivity (95).

prepare_test88.Builder (alloc/refexpr/kind/lin/eqpair/check/cases) emits raw step dicts; prepare_test23.run_checks emits the ordered obligation list (domain, rows, objective, then projection observations) and the Return map, both by hand.

prepare_test19.cases_le wraps local Cases; menu_injectivity.split_expression builds the integer Witness split; prepare_test40.expression/row_fact/plus/mul/substitute do the exact arithmetic; prepare_test57.substitute re-maps row facts.
No kernel-side constructor is used: claims and blocks are Python dicts serialized as 'RPA 7' plus compact JSON, and request.json is a second dump of the same claims array.
friction: No public proof-construction API: the whole certificate is hand-built dicts sitting on an 8-module, 1,392-line helper stack that was lifted from sibling case preparers rather than provided by the kernel.

Failure attribution: the four mutated certificates return only messages ('INVALID missing obligation', 'INVALID obligation mismatch: expected Le; obligation 11278' out of 161,364) with no claim, block, step or coordinate.

The same retained-coordinate contract is retyped four times (5,677 pairs and about 22,685 coordinate facts per claim) and the same claims array is emitted twice (proof.rpa and request.json), held consistent only by hand assertions.
The deleted set is re-derived by a name diff against the target and asserted (tools/prepare_test13.py:34); nothing binds the audit's edit list to the target's actual coordinate and row diff.
The single failed tool call of the run was 'import networkx' (digest test13.md:537,565), after which Tarjan SCC had to be written by hand for the 69 alias groups.
